verdict.rationale: cubic lets users define rules that run automatically on pull-request events. Custom agents are user-defined review rules applied across PRs, configurable in cubic.yaml. Toggles act on PR events without manual action: auto-approval against a review policy, auto-fix on every review, and auto-resolve threads. However, these are fixed, built-in event-to-action behaviors scoped to code review, not a general rules engine where users pick triggers and actions. missing for 10: user-definable arbitrary event triggers and custom action chaining beyond review/approve/fix/resolve, a documented rule syntax for event-to-action mappings, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
Custom agents are review rules that enforce your organization's specific best practices across pull requests.
`cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
Enable [auto-approval](/ai-review/auto-approval) to let cubic approve PRs that meet your review policy.
turn on auto-fix to have cubic fix the issues from every review of a pull request.
Enable automatic thread resolution to close findings when the issue is fixed
